reason: The server encountered an unexpected condition that prevented it from fulfilling the request. Often caused by unhandled exceptions in the backend route or database timeout.
fix: Check backend application logs for stack traces.
Ensure database connections are alive.
Wrap asynchronous route handlers in robust try/catch blocks.

reason: The client made a request that the server cannot process. This typically means a broken API endpoint, missing authorization headers, or malformed JSON payloads.
fix: Validate the request payload format strictly matches the backend schema.
Verify that the Authorization headers (e.g. Bearer token) are pushed correctly.
Check if the API endpoint URL in the frontend fetch/axios call is correct.

reason: The user is attempting to access a protected route without a valid authentication token, or the token has expired.
fix: Check local storage/cookies for the presence of a valid JWT or session token.
Redirect the user to the login page if the token is null.
Implement a token refresh interceptor in your HTTP client.

reason: The user is authenticated but does not have the correct administrative or role-based permissions to access this resource.
fix: Verify the user's role array matches the route requirements.
Ensure the backend middleware correctly parses and applies authorization scopes.
Hide UI elements that the user cannot interact with.

reason: The requested API endpoint or dynamic route parameter does not exist on the server.
fix: Verify the spelling and path of the requested URL.
Ensure dynamic route parameters (like IDs) actually correspond to existing database records.
Add a global 404 fallback route in the backend.

reason: The browser blocked the fetch request because the backend server did not return the required Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers.
fix: Install the 'cors' package in your backend.
Whitelist the exact frontend domain (e.g. localhost:5173).
Ensure preflight OPTIONS requests are handled successfully.

reason: Anchor tags (<a>) on the DOM point to routes that return 404 Not Found, creating structural dead-ends for the user and search engines.
fix: Identify the broken href attributes in your site navigation or footer.
Redirect deprecated URLs to their modern equivalents using 301 redirects.
Implement a link-checking step in your CI/CD pipeline.
remediationCode: Valid Link Destination

reason: JavaScript encountered a null or undefined reference during a property lookup. This breaks interactive UI components across the page.
fix: Implement optional chaining (?.) on deeply nested object structures.
Add null-checks before mapping arrays or accessing DOM elements.
Utilize TypeScript for stronger compile-time type guarantees.

reason: Code attempted to access a variable that has not been declared or is out of scope.
fix: Ensure all variables are declared with let/const before use.
Check for typos in variable or function names.
Verify that external scripts or modules have loaded properly.

reason: The JavaScript engine encountered invalid language syntax, typically a missing brace, comma, or parenthesis, preventing execution entirely.
fix: Check your bundler (Webpack/Vite) output for compilation errors.
Ensure all JSON strings are properly quoted and valid.
Look for orphaned brackets in the specified file line.

reason: An asynchronous operation failed, but no '.catch()' block or 'try/catch' was provided to gracefully handle the error.
fix: Wrap all await calls inside try/catch blocks.
Append .catch() to all raw Promise chains.
Provide user feedback (toasts/alerts) when an async UI action fails.

reason: Elements dynamically loaded into the DOM without predefined dimensions caused massive layout repaints.
fix: Define standard aspect ratios or fixed dimensions for ALL images and iframes.
Pre-allocate space for dynamic banners or ads.
Load fonts pre-emptively to avoid text flashing.

reason: Elements lack ARIA labels, semantic structure, or keyboard interactivity, making the site hostile to screen readers.
fix: Provide robust 'aria-label' or 'alt' attributes to all non-text elements.
Ensure interactive elements (divs acting as buttons) have 'tabIndex=0' and keydown listeners.
Refactor non-semantic layouts to use <nav>, <main>, and <article> tags.
remediationCode:
<!-- Replace a div button with semantic HTML or proper ARIA -->
<button 
  onClick={handleAction}
  aria-label="Submit Form Data"
  className="btn-primary">
  Submit
</button>

reason: Document parsing exceeded 3000ms. Often caused by unoptimized images, render-blocking scripts, or a bloated main thread.
fix: Implement lazy-loading for offscreen images and heavy components.
Minify and compress your distribution bundles via gzip or brotli.
Deploy static assets via a global Edge CDN.

reason: The browser blocked requests to insecure HTTP URLs while the main application is running on secure HTTPS.
fix: Use protocol-relative URLs (starting with //) or explicitly rewrite all HTTP to HTTPS.
Configure your web server to redirect HTTP traffic to HTTPS via a 301.
Add the 'Content-Security-Policy: upgrade-insecure-requests' header.
remediationCode:
<!-- Apply meta tag to upgrade insecure assets automatically -->
<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="upgrade-insecure-requests">

reason: A critical deviation from standard front-end or endpoint security protocols has been logged.
fix: Implement rate-limiting to block brute-force attempts.
Sanitize output immediately before rendering to the DOM to prevent XSS.
Ensure secure cookies with HttpOnly and SameSite flags.

reason: Images without alt attributes are invisible to screen readers, making the content inaccessible to visually impaired users.
fix: Add a descriptive 'alt' attribute to all tags.
For decorative images, use an empty alt attribute (alt="").
Ensure the alt text actually describes the image content.

reason: Interactive elements (buttons, inputs) are disabled without providing feedback or a way for the user to understand why, which causes frustration.
fix: Add a tooltip or hint explaining why the element is disabled.
Use 'aria-disabled="true"' instead of the 'disabled' attribute if the element should remain focusable.
Ensure disabled states have sufficient color contrast.
remediationCode:
<!-- Use aria-disabled for better accessibility feedback -->
<button 
  aria-disabled="true" 
  title="Please complete all required fields first" 
  className="opacity-50 cursor-not-allowed">
  Submit
</button>

reason: A navigation link points to a destination that no longer exists (404), leading to a 'dead end' for both users and crawlers.
fix: Identify the dead href and update it to the correct destination.
If the page has moved permanently, implement a 301 redirect on the server.
Remove legacy links that are no longer relevant to the site mapping.

reason: The Strict-Transport-Security header is missing, which prevents the browser from enforcing HTTPS usage, leaving the user vulnerable to SSL stripping attacks.
fix: Add the Strict-Transport-Security header to all server responses.
Set a max-age of at least 31536000 seconds (1 year).
Include the includeSubDomains directive for full domain protection.

reason: The X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header is missing, allowing browsers to MIME-sniff the response away from the declared content-type, which can lead to script injection.
fix: Add the X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header to your backend configuration.
In Express, use helmet.noSniff() middleware.
remediationCode:
const helmet = require('helmet');
app.use(helmet.noSniff());

reason: The Referrer-Policy header defines how much referrer information (sent via the Referer header) should be included with requests.
fix: Implement a strict Referrer-Policy like 'same-origin' or 'no-referrer'.
In Express, use helmet.referrerPolicy() to set a safe default.
remediationCode:
const helmet = require('helmet');
app.use(helmet.referrerPolicy({ policy: 'same-origin' }));
